T0.reason: Draw calls re-recorded for P3-T16, which made the harness measure two things it had been missing. (1) `populate` assigned owner with `i % 2` against a FOUR-type unit mix, so type and owner were perfectly correlated and every unit mesh was counted for one side only — the exact bias that understated ADR-0016's own batch figures until P3-T02 re-measured them. Decorrelated, which is +4. (2) The harness kept its own extractor and ran it AFTER `bridge.step` had drained `state.events`, so no death ever reached it and the `blast` overlay never fired; it reads the bridge's snapshot now, which is +1 and also removes a second full extraction per tick the game never pays for. Both are the gate becoming more honest, not the frame becoming more expensive. p95 untouched. T0: 17 -> 22.

P3.reason: PRD §5's Phase 3 combat scene, and the gate ADR-0016 named as its own supersede trigger. Every unit type on the field at once, both sides packed into weapons range so shots and deaths actually happen — the other scenes use the four-type MVP mix, which meant none of ADR-0016's nine new silhouettes had ever reached a perf gate. 43 draw calls: 39 batches (15 unit meshes x 2 owners, plus buildings, imposters and a deposit), terrain, and four overlay layers. p95 is NULL on purpose: it has not been recorded on a machine worth trusting. This container reports figures 1.7x the CI runner's on identical commits, and writing one in would arm the regression check against noise. The scene is still gated on the PRD's own 33 ms budget, which is machine-independent, and on its draw-call count, which is structural. Record a p95 from a CI run before relying on the regression half.
